content.user_title: Review TypeScript Changes Against Metabase Standards
content.value_statement: TypeScript reviews can miss project rules, accessibility issues, and performance regressions. This skill applies Metabase standards and prioritizes actionable findings.
actual_capabilities: Reviews TypeScript and JavaScript pull request diffs against Metabase coding standards.
Prioritizes linked typescript-write rules, including prohibited explicit or implicit any usage.
Checks type modeling, null handling, naming, structure, comments, and maintainability.
Flags testing, accessibility, performance, security, bundle size, and analytics concerns.
Uses language server evidence when verifying prohibited any types.
limitations: Depends on repository guidance files that are not included in this skill package.
Does not replace automated tests, type checking, linting, or dedicated security analysis.
Provides review findings but does not modify code or create fixes automatically.
Metabase-specific rules may not suit unrelated TypeScript projects.

use_cases.title: Review a frontend pull request
use_cases.description: Check a TypeScript diff for blocking standards violations and secondary quality concerns before requesting review.

use_cases.title: Prioritize review findings
use_cases.description: Sort code review feedback by project rules, maintainability, testing, accessibility, performance, security, and product instrumentation.

use_cases.title: Audit team review coverage
use_cases.description: Identify recurring blind spots across frontend changes, including bundle impact, analytics events, and keyboard accessibility.

prompt_templates.title: Basic diff review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this TypeScript diff. List blocking issues first, then testing, accessibility, performance, security, bundle size, and analytics concerns.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a focused first review of a small change.

prompt_templates.title: Standards compliance review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these JavaScript and TypeScript changes against Metabase standards. Cite affected files and explain each recommended change.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when project conventions are the primary concern.

prompt_templates.title: Frontend risk review
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this frontend pull request for type safety, test gaps, accessibility, performance, security, bundle growth, and missing analytics events.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a feature that changes user-facing behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced prioritized review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the complete diff and rank findings by severity. Separate blocking standards violations from additive concerns and note uncertain conclusions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for large or complex pull requests requiring triage.

output_examples.input: A form adds an icon-only submit button and uses an explicit any type.
output: Blocking: replace the explicit any type with a precise model and verify it with the language server.
Accessibility: give the icon-only button an accessible name and confirm keyboard behavior.

output_examples.input: A new route imports a large utility package and adds a modal without tracking.
output: Bundle size: import only the required utility or load the heavy dependency with the route.
Analytics: confirm whether opening and completing the new modal flow require tracking events.

output_examples.input: A typed refactor preserves behavior and includes focused tests.
output_examples.output: No blocking issues found. The types are specific, behavior is covered, and no additional accessibility or performance concern is evident.

best_practices: Provide the complete diff and relevant repository context for accurate findings.
Run type checks, tests, and linting before using the skill for final review.
Validate blocking findings against the linked Metabase guidance and language server output.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill as the only security or accessibility review.
Do not apply Metabase-specific rules to unrelated repositories without adapting the standards.
Do not treat every suggestion as blocking when the skill marks concerns as additive.

faq.question: Which languages does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews TypeScript and JavaScript changes, with emphasis on Metabase frontend conventions.

faq.question: Does it edit source code?
faq.answer: No. It produces prioritized review findings and recommended changes.

faq.question: Can it replace TypeScript checks and linting?
faq.answer: No. Run automated checks because the skill relies on repository context and review evidence.

faq.question: What findings are treated as blocking?
faq.answer: Violations of the linked typescript-write rules receive highest priority, especially new explicit or implicit any types.

faq.question: Does it review React accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks keyboard support, focus handling, accessible names, semantic controls, modal focus traps, and linked form labels.

faq.question: Can it review non-Metabase projects?
faq.answer: It can inspect them, but its standards and priorities are specific to the Metabase repository.
